newsitem.title: USA: Minn. unemployment rate falls to 3.1 pct in July.
newsitem.headline: Minn. unemployment rate falls to 3.1 pct in July.

text.p: Minnesota Gov. Arne Carlson announced Thursday that the state's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate dropped one percentage point in July to 3.1 percent.
Minnesota set a record low unemployment rate for the second consecutive month and also set an all-time high for employment statewide based on calculation methods adopted in 1978, Carlson said.
The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate was 4.1 percent in July 1996.
The national seasonally adjusted rate was 4.8 percent in July, compared to 5 percent in June and 5.4 percent a year ago.
